decisionsTitle: A backoffice table's columns can be resized: the one cost `AdminTable`'s refusal named, paid without the Data Grid
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-03, from the phone:** «tabelele ar trebui să folosească MUI Data Grid ca să pot face resize la coloane». What he wants is to resize columns. The data grid was refused when `AdminTable` was built, for four reasons its docstring records and that all still hold: it is a Client Component, so every participant row would cross the server boundary as a prop (`AGENTS.md` §14.5); sorting, filtering and paging would move from the URL into client memory, so a filtered list could no longer be bookmarked or come back after a Server Action redirects; its free tier pages on the client; and the lists would stop working with JavaScript off. That refusal named «no column resizing» as its price. This decision pays that price inside `AdminTable`, with no dependency, and keeps the four reasons.

**Decision.**
- `AdminTable` takes a `tableId` (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; checked, because it becomes a storage key and a CSS selector). Every list names its own: `events`, `pages`, `albums-event`, `albums-free`, `pictures`, `staff`, `registrations`, and one per legal text (`legal-privacy-notice`, …).
- The table stays server-rendered. It now emits a `<colgroup>` with one `<col data-column>` per column, the row verbs' last, hidden at the same breakpoints as their cells, so the colgroup and the cells always count the same columns.
- Each heading carries one small client island, `ColumnResizeHandle`: the column's right edge, a focusable `role="separator"` (the window-splitter pattern). A pointer drags it; the arrow keys move it 16 px, Shift 64, Home to the column's own floor and End to 960 px; a double click puts that one column back. Its `aria-valuenow` (and `aria-valuetext`, «240 px») is the column's width as laid out now, said again whenever the table is laid out — after a reload with stored widths, a reset, a double click, a breakpoint — not only after a drag; `aria-valuemin` is the floor. It receives strings only — the table's id, the column's key, its heading — and lays the table out through the DOM. No row, no render function and no participant data crosses to the client.
- No heading word is ever cut. Each column has a floor of its own, measured in the browser while the heading is still one line: the heading's longest word, plus what stays beside the words (the sort arrow, a hint) and the cell's padding — never under 56 px. A drag, the arrows and Home stop there, and a stored width under it (the other language's longer word) is raised to it. Once a table is resized its headings wrap between words only.
- A resized table switches to `table-layout: fixed` at the sum of its columns: a column nobody dragged keeps the width the automatic layout gives it on today's rows; a long value wraps inside its column and a body cell clips what still does not fit. Wider than the frame, the frame scrolls sideways inside its own border, never the page.
- The widths are this browser's own, per table, in `localStorage` under `br.table.<id>.widths` (only the columns somebody dragged; an empty entry is removed; a storage that refuses, as in some private windows, reads as nothing stored and the drag still works on the page). A preference about one screen is not something the server, the URL or another organiser needs; a cookie per table read on every request was refused for the same reason. The cost: the server's HTML paints once before the stored widths apply, so a resized table settles a moment after the first paint (they apply in a layout effect, in the frame the handles appear).
- Under the table, `ColumnWidths` re-applies the stored widths on load, whenever the table's frame changes width (a breakpoint crossed, a fold opened) and when another tab changes them, and shows «Lățimi implicite» / «Default widths» only while something is stored, from `md` up; pressing it hands the keyboard's focus to the table's first column edge.
- With JavaScript off neither island draws anything and the table is exactly the automatic one it was. The phone layout has no columns and is untouched (race morning is a phone, `AGENTS.md` §18.5).
- The handle's reach is 16 px under a mouse, centred on the edge, and 44 px under a finger (`pointer: coarse`, BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 6), 28 of them on its own side and 16 past the edge — both stay inside the next heading's 16 px of padding, so that heading's sort link keeps its pixels. The visible line is drawn for a mouse only (`pointer: fine`).

**Refused.** `@mui/x-data-grid` (above; if the owner still wants the grid after seeing this, that is a separate decision). `@mui/x-data-grid`'s column resizing has been MIT since v7; the grid is refused for the four reasons above, not its licence. Resizing on the phone layout (blocks per row, no columns): there is nothing to resize, and race morning is a phone. Drag-reordering and keyboard navigation between cells stay unbuilt and are still named as the price in `AdminTable`. Widths stored on the server per staff member: a migration and a write per drag, for a preference about one screen. Proportions instead of pixels (§271 stores proportions for a page's table, written once and read at every width; this is one person's own screen, and a proportion would move every other column the moment one was dragged).

Code: `src/modules/staff-identity/ui/AdminTable.tsx` (the docstring amended), `ColumnResizeHandle.tsx`, `ColumnWidths.tsx`, `column-widths-dom.ts`, `domain/column-widths.ts`; the words in `Admin.columns`, carried to the backoffice's islands by `src/i18n/client-messages.ts`. Tests: `tests/unit/staff/admin-table-column-widths.test.ts` (the arithmetic, each column's floor, the server markup, and the storage with a fake and a refusing `localStorage`), `tests/e2e/admin-column-widths.spec.ts` (a drag on the registrations list at 1280 px, the reload, the reset, the arrow key's `aria-valuenow`, and no edge at 320 px).
changelogLine: - **The backoffice tables' columns can be resized** — drag a column's edge in any list (or focus it and use the arrow keys); a column never goes narrower than its heading's longest word, this browser remembers the widths per table, and «Lățimi implicite» puts them back. The tables are still drawn on the server and still work without JavaScript. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a backoffice list at `md` and up with JavaScript on, when a column's edge is dragged or moved with the arrow keys, then that column takes the new width (from its own floor — its heading's longest word with its arrow and padding, never under 56 px — to 960 px, so no heading word is cut), the table switches to a fixed layout whose other columns keep their width, the frame scrolls sideways inside its border rather than the page, and the width is kept for that table in that browser (`br.table.<id>.widths`) until «Lățimi implicite» or a double click on the edge; the edge is a focusable separator whose `aria-valuenow` is the column's width as laid out now, from the first focus; with JavaScript off, and on the phone layout, no edge and no reset control is drawn and the table is the automatic one; the edge reaches 44 px under a finger without covering the next heading's sort link; the islands receive the table's id, the column's key and its heading, never a row (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
